## Purpose
`economy.ts`'s `SavingsSource` and `specs.ts`'s `SpecChild.source` field are the subproject's two "provenance" vocabularies: a closed string-literal set naming WHERE a value/row came from (which savings intervention produced it; which scan discovered a sub-spec link). Both mirror a Rust-side enum/union one-to-one and both are documented with a per-variant JSDoc explaining what each value means in practice, since the bare string gives no clue on its own.

## Convention
Folder: apps/dashboard/src/lib/types/** · Extension: .ts · Files of this role in this subproject: 2
`economy.ts` declares a standalone named type, `export type SavingsSource = "rtk_rewrite" | "model_routing_downgrade" | ...;`, used as a field type elsewhere (`SavingsBySource.source: SavingsSource`). `specs.ts` instead inlines the union directly on the field (`source?: "event" | "header" | "both";`) without extracting a named type, because the union is small, used in exactly one place, and the field's optionality (backwards compatibility with older payloads) is itself part of the documented contract — worth keeping visible on the field rather than hidden behind a type alias. Both spellings appear in this subproject; the read exemplars don't establish a single house rule for when to extract vs. inline.

## How to apply
Extract a standalone `export type XSource = "a" | "b" | ...;` (matching `SavingsSource`) when the same source vocabulary is reused across more than one interface/field. Inline the union directly on the field (matching `SpecChild.source`) when it's local to one DTO and especially when it's optional for backwards compatibility — document each variant's meaning in a JSDoc block above the field either way, since these strings never carry meaning by themselves.
